name: Backdrop blur
summary: A translucent layer that blurs what is behind it, so that a panel reads as frosted glass over the content.
how: Blur the backdrop by 10 to 40 px.
Give the panel a white or black tint of 10% to 40% opacity.
Add a 1 px light edge at 20% to 50% opacity to show the edge of the glass.

origin.note: iOS 7 puts the control centre and the menus on blurred, translucent layers.

adoptions.via: CSS backdrop-filter reaches the main browsers, and web pages take up frosted panels.
Apple's Liquid Glass adds refraction and bright edges to the blurred layer.

sources.title: W3C, Filter Effects Module Level 2: backdrop-filter
